Afghan left-arm pacer Fazalhaq Farooqi became the most expensive player in ILT20 auction history on October 1, 2026, when MI Emirates secured him for USD 380,000 at the Season 5 Player Auction in Dubai. This landmark bid at the ICC Academy Indoors surpassed the previous benchmark of USD 260,000, set by Andre Fletcher for MI Emirates during the Season 4 auction, marking a USD 120,000 increase and underscoring a sharp rise in demand for elite fast bowlers.

The day was particularly dynamic as the auction record changed hands three times. Gulf Giants initially set a new high by securing Rahmanullah Gurbaz for USD 310,000 via a Right-to-Match card. They then further escalated the bidding, acquiring Liam Livingstone for USD 350,000. However, Farooqi's USD 380,000 hammer price ultimately closed the day as the definitive high-water mark, reflecting MI Emirates' aggressive strategy, which saw them spend a total of USD 2,000,000.

Beyond the top bids, Dubai Capitals signed Faf du Plessis for USD 300,000, while Gulf Giants added Alzarri Joseph for USD 230,000. MI Emirates also made Muhammad Waseem the highest-priced UAE player, retaining him for USD 210,000 via a Right-to-Match card. Desert Vipers assembled a Pakistan-heavy group, picking up Babar Azam, Naseem Shah, Fakhar Zaman, and Shadab Khan, each at the USD 80,000 base price, with Babar set to make his ILT20 debut.

Hundreds of students from Lady Shri Ram College for Women (LSR) gathered outside its back gate, extending to Moolchand, following the incident. A police encounter near LSR's back gate even led to temporary online classes. Students report frequent issues like catcalling, stalking, and indecent exposure. Anjali, a Gargi College alumna, recounted changing her route from Moolchand Metro Station to Green Park Station due to men following her on deserted paths, despite the added time and cost. The eight-to-nine-minute walk from Moolchand Metro to LSR’s back gate is deemed unsafe after dark due to poor lighting and low footfall.

Students are advocating for systemic improvements rather than imposing restrictions on their movement. During the LSR solidarity march, participants walked along routes they identified as unsafe, from the back gate towards Moolchand. While policing at LSR has increased post-incident, including activity at the Pink Booth, students question why these measures were not implemented before such a "heinous crime" occurred. The Students’ Union has addressed issues like unlit roads, lack of policing, and blocked footpaths.

Voting took place on Monday, September 28, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with vote counting extending until 3 a.m. the following day. Dilshada Raihan VP, pursuing a Ph.D. in Philosophy and representing the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), was elected president, securing a margin of over 450 votes against ABVP candidate Naresh P. The winning Left alliance comprises the All India Students’ Association (AISA), Ambedkar Students’ Association (ASA), Democratic Students’ Union (DSU), SFI, and Tribal Student’s Forum (TSF). Other key office bearers include Korra Nithin Chauhan as Vice-President and Pratik Sagar as General Secretary.

Of the six executive positions in the central panel, five were won by the Left combine. Banoth Sai, from IMSC Chemistry, was the sole victor for ABVP-SLVD as Sports Secretary. Additionally, Vislavath Jiyasherin from IMA Political Science, also from ABVP-SLVD, was elected to the Internal Complaints Committee (Gender Sensitization Committee Against Sexual Harassment). This year's outcome represents a significant reversal from the 2025–26 elections, when ABVP had secured all six executive positions.

UN Rapporteur Questions Civilian Deaths in Pakistan Airstrikes in Afghanistan

UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Afghanistan, Richard Bennett, has called for accountability regarding recent Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan, which he stated appeared to violate international human rights and humanitarian law. The United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) confirmed that at least 10 civilians, predominantly children, were killed in strikes across Kunar and Helmand provinces, with nine others injured. Bennett questioned the circumstances, stating, "Is this incompetence, negligence or worse? Whatever, there is no justification for doing such irreparable harm to civilians."

The Taliban government reported a slightly different toll, citing nine people killed and 11 injured after three houses were hit, with women and children among the casualties, condemning the act as "aggression and crime." Conversely, Pakistan's information ministry maintained that the strikes were based on "credible intelligence," targeting militant hideouts at two locations, and initial reports suggested the killing of 22 terrorists, alongside the destruction of weapons and ammunition stores.

These airstrikes mark a fresh escalation of tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, following nearly three months of calm. The renewed hostilities began after a militant attack in northwestern Pakistan last month killed 24 people. Islamabad frequently accuses Kabul of harbouring militants who launch cross-border attacks, an allegation the Taliban government consistently rejects, instead characterizing militancy as Pakistan's internal issue.

What to watch: Further investigations into civilian casualties and diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions between the two nations.

FINANCE · Livemint Money · editor 9/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

EPFO Enrolment Campaign 2026 Opens for Workers Left Outside PF

The Employees’ Enrolment Campaign 2026 (EEC 2026) has opened a one‑time window for salaried workers who were eligible for the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) but remained outside the formal system between 1 April 2009 and 31 March 2026. Employers can bring these workers under EPF coverage until 31 October 2026 by filing a declaration.

To qualify, the employee must be alive and still employed with the establishment at the time of declaration. The employer pays a nominal fee, deposits its share of EPF from the employee’s declared date of joining, and adds applicable interest, administrative charges and a ₹100 lump‑sum damage.

A key relief is that the employee’s share of EPF contributions is waived if those contributions were not deducted from wages in the past. Consequently, workers who were not covered will retain both their contributions and the interest that would have accrued, avoiding any loss.

Workers who exited the establishment before the declaration cannot be declared under the campaign, and no suo‑motu compliance action will be taken against them if the employer submits the prescribed undertaking. Employers must generate a UAN via the UMANG app, remit contributions through the Electronic Challan‑cum‑Return platform, and conduct an internal audit to identify eligible employees.

SCIENCE · Phys.org · editor 9/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Webb Telescope Identifies Rare Extreme Debris Disks from Planetary Collisions

Astronomers using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope have identified a rare class of stellar systems known as extreme debris disks, offering insights into violent planet-forming collisions. Published in The Astrophysical Journal, the study led by Kate Su of the Space Science Institute in Boulder, Colorado, compiled a sample of 21 such disks, including 16 observed by Webb. These systems are characterized by unusually large amounts of warm dust close to their host stars, a phase estimated to occur in only about 1% of young stars.

The research reveals that these disks are not uniform but split into two distinct categories based on mineralogical makeup. Approximately one-third of the sample is silica-rich, indicating high-energy impacts between Mars-sized bodies that vaporized significant material. These silica-rich disks are found only around stars younger than 300 million years. The remaining two-thirds are silica-poor, suggesting smaller-scale collisions between moon-sized objects. These silica-poor disks persist across a broader range of ages and exhibit greater irregular brightness variations, likely driven by rapid orbital changes and fresh debris.

Agnes Kospal of Konkoly Observatory in Budapest, Hungary, noted that Webb’s mid-infrared spectra were crucial for identifying these compositions, as the planetary embryos themselves are too small to study directly. The findings align with simulations suggesting terrestrial planets form within the first few hundred million years of a solar system’s existence. This timeline supports the theory that Earth and the moon formed around 100 million years after the sun formed, potentially resulting from a collision with a Mars-sized object.

What to watch: Future observations of silica-poor disks may clarify the role of orbital instability in the Late Heavy Bombardment hypothesis.

Source: Phys.org · permalink · more science

The mission, designated Crew-13, follows a three-week delay caused by a leaking fuel system in the Dragon capsule. Commander Jessica Watkins, the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit, is joined by NASA’s Luke Delaney, Canada’s Joshua Kutryk, and Russia’s Sergey Teteryatnikov. Joshua Kutryk is expected to become the fourth astronaut to become a father while in orbit, with his wife Heather due to give birth in late November. The crew carried a small crocheted dragon named 'Lucky' to commemorate their mission, which pays homage to the historic Apollo 13. This launch marked the 13th crew SpaceX has sent for NASA.
